{"content":"Proofs of the Obligations in obligations.txt — Natural Deduction

1. PRELIMINARIES

1.1 Notation
    e, e0, ...   expressions            n, m          integer literals
    value(e)     e is a literal         ->, ->*       as in semantics.txt
    [phi]        assumption phi         []            end of proof
    ND rules:    &I &E  (and intro/elim),  |I |E  (or intro/elim),
                 =>I =>E (implication),    ~I ~E  (negation),
                 forallI forallE,          existsI existsE,
                 RAA (reductio),           IND (structural induction),
                 |E with cited subproofs for each disjunct.
    Notation for formulas: & = and, | = or, ~ = not, => = implies.

1.2 Closure lemmas for ->* (by definition of the reflexive-
    transitive closure; used without further comment)
    CL1  e ->* e                                  (reflexivity)
    CL2  e ->* f & f ->* g  =>  e ->* g           (transitivity)
    CL3  e -> f  =>  e ->* f                      (monotonicity)

1.3 Background facts about Z (standard ordered-ring properties,
    used as premises)
    AF1  (trichotomy)          forall n in Z:  n < 0 | n = 0 | n > 0
    AF2  (irreflexivity)       forall n:  ~(n < n)
    AF3  (mixed transitivity)  a < b & b <= c  =>  a < c
    AF4  (negation reverses)   n < 0  =>  -n > 0
    AF5  (definition of >=)    n >= 0  <=>  n > 0 | n = 0
    AF6  (totality)            + and unary - are total functions on
                               Z with unique results; hence n1 + n2
                               and -n are literals of Expr.

    Remark: the grammar of semantics.txt has no variables, so every
    expression is closed.

2. LEMMA L1 (VALUE-IRREDUCIBILITY)

    L1:  forall n. ~exists e'. n -> e'

1. [n -> e']                                  Assumption
2. A derivation of n -> e' ends in a rule whose conclusion's left
   side matches the literal n. Left sides of the rules (sec. 3,
   semantics.txt): abs(e) [S-ABS], e1 + e2 [S-ADD-L], n + e2
   [S-ADD-R], n1 + n2 [R-ADD], abs(n) [R-ABS-POS/NEG]. None is a
   literal.                                   rule schemas
3. No rule instance has left side n; no derivation exists.   2
4. F                                          1, 3
5. ~exists e'. n -> e'                        1-4, ~I
6. forall n. ~exists e'. n -> e'              5, forallI
[]

3. OBLIGATIONS O1, O2, O3

O1a (side conditions well-formed)
1. The side conditions are "n >= 0", "n < 0", "n3 = n1 + n2":
   atomic formulas of first-order arithmetic with all variables
   ranging over Z.                            sec. 3, semantics.txt
2. Each is a well-formed proposition.         1, definitional
[]

O1b (smallest rule-closed relation exists)
1. Let R = { S subset of Expr x Expr : S is closed under all rules }.
2. Expr x Expr is in R: for any rule instance with true side
   condition and premises in Expr x Expr, the conclusion is an
   element of Expr x Expr.                    trivially
3. R is nonempty.                             2
4. ->  :=  intersection of R.                 3, set comprehension
5. -> is closed under the rules: given premises in -> and a true
   side condition, the conclusion lies in every S in R (each S is
   closed), hence in the intersection.        4, definition of intersection
6. -> is the smallest such relation: any closed S satisfies
   intersection of R subset of S.             4, definition of intersection
7. -> exists and is smallest.                 2-6, existsI
[]  (O1 discharged by O1a and O1b.)

O2 (CASE-COVERAGE):  forall n in Z. n >= 0 | n < 0

1. [n in Z]                                   Assumption
2. n < 0 | n = 0 | n > 0                      AF1
3. Case n < 0:   n < 0                        right disjunct, |I
4. Case n = 0:   n >= 0                       2 (n = 0), AF5, =-substitution
5. Case n > 0:   n >= 0                       AF5
6. n >= 0 | n < 0                             2-5, |E
7. forall n in Z. n >= 0 | n < 0              1-6, forallI
[]

O3 (CASE-DISJOINTNESS):  forall n. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)

1. [n >= 0 & n < 0]                           Assumption
2. n >= 0, i.e. 0 <= n                        &E 1
3. n < 0                                      &E 1
4. n < n                                      AF3 on 3, 2
5. ~(n < n)                                   AF2
6. F                                          4, 5, ~E
7. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)                          1-6, ~I
8. forall n. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)                7, forallI
[]

4. LEMMAS L2, L3

L2 (PROGRESS-EXPR):  forall e. value(e) | exists e'. e -> e'
    Proof by IND on e.

Case e = n:
1. value(n)                                   def. of value
2. value(n) | exists e'. n -> e'              1, |I

Case e = abs(e0), with IH: value(e0) | exists e'. e0 -> e':
1. Case value(e0), i.e. e0 = n:
   1.1 n >= 0 | n < 0                         O2
   1.2 Case n >= 0: abs(n) -> n               R-ABS-POS
       Case n < 0:  abs(n) -> -n              R-ABS-NEG
   1.3 exists e'. abs(e0) -> e'               1.2, |E, existsI
   1.4 disjunction                            1.3, |I
2. Case e0 -> e0':  abs(e0) -> abs(e0')       S-ABS
   existsI; |I
3. value(abs(e0)) | exists e'. abs(e0) -> e'  1-2, |E

Case e = e1 + e2, with IH(e1), IH(e2):
1. Case e1 -> e1':  e1 + e2 -> e1' + e2       S-ADD-L; existsI; |I
2. Case value(e1), i.e. e1 = n1:
   2.1 Case e2 -> e2': n1 + e2 -> n1 + e2'    S-ADD-R; existsI; |I
   2.2 Case value(e2), i.e. e2 = n2:
       n1 + n2 -> n3, where n3 = n1 + n2      R-ADD, AF6 (totality)
       existsI; |I
3. disjunction                                1-2, |E

All three cases give the disjunction; IND discharges the induction.
[]

L3 (DETERMINISM-EXPR):  forall e a b. (e -> a & e -> b) => a = b
    Proof by IND on e, with case analysis on applicable rules.

Case e = n:
1. [n -> a & n -> b]                          Assumption
2. F                                          1, L1 (no step from n)
3. a = b                                      2, RAA (vacuous)

Case e = abs(e0), with IH for e0. Rules matching abs(_): S-ABS,
R-ABS-POS, R-ABS-NEG.
1. Case value(e0), i.e. e0 = n:
   1.1 S-ABS inapplicable: its premise n -> c contradicts L1.
   1.2 R-ABS-POS and R-ABS-NEG cannot both apply: their side
       conditions n >= 0 and n < 0 together contradict O3.
   1.3 Exactly one of R-ABS-POS, R-ABS-NEG applies (O2, 1.2), and
       its conclusion is fully determined (n, resp. -n). Hence
       a = b.
2. Case ~value(e0):
   2.1 R-ABS-POS/NEG inapplicable: their schemas require the
       argument to be a literal; e0 is not. (schema mismatch)
   2.2 Only S-ABS applies: a = abs(c), b = abs(d) with e0 -> c,
       e0 -> d.
   2.3 c = d                                  IH
   2.4 a = b                                  2.2, 2.3

Case e = e1 + e2, with IH for e1, e2. Rules matching _ + _: S-ADD-L,
S-ADD-R, R-ADD.
1. Case ~value(e1): only S-ADD-L applies (S-ADD-R and R-ADD require
   e1 to be a literal). a = c + e2, b = d + e2 with e1 -> c,
   e1 -> d; c = d by IH; hence a = b.
2. Case e1 = n1, ~value(e2): S-ADD-L blocked (premise n1 -> _
   contradicts L1); only S-ADD-R: a = b = n1 + e2' (uniqueness of
   e2' by IH).
3. Case e1 = n1, e2 = n2: S-ADD-L and S-ADD-R blocked by L1; only
   R-ADD: a = n1 + n2 = b by AF6 (functionality).

All cases: a = b; IND discharges the induction.
[]

5. OBLIGATIONS O4 THROUGH O11 AND O0

O4 (PROGRESS-ABS):  forall e. value(abs(e)) | exists e'. abs(e) -> e'
1. value(abs(e)) is false: values are literals and abs(_) is
   syntactically not a literal.               sec. 1, semantics.txt
2. L2: value(e) | exists e'. e -> e'
3. Case e = n:
   3.1 n >= 0 | n < 0                         O2
   3.2 Case n >= 0: abs(n) -> n               R-ABS-POS
       Case n < 0:  abs(n) -> -n              R-ABS-NEG
   3.3 exists e'. abs(e) -> e'                3.2, |E, existsI
4. Case e -> e': abs(e) -> abs(e')            S-ABS; existsI
5. value(abs(e)) | exists e'. abs(e) -> e'    3, 4, |I (right)
6. forall e. ...                              5, forallI
[]

O5 (DETERMINISM-ABS):  (abs(e) -> a & abs(e) -> b) => a = b
1. L3, case e = abs(e0), derives exactly this statement.
2. forall e. (abs(e) -> a & abs(e) -> b) => a = b    1, forallI
[]

O6 (VALUE-CORR-POS):  n >= 0 => ((abs(n) ->* m & value(m)) => m = n)

1. [n >= 0]                                   Assumption
2. abs(n) -> n                                R-ABS-POS (side cond. 1)
3. abs(n) ->* n                               2, CL3
4. [abs(n) ->* m & value(m)]                  Assumption
5. abs(n) = e0 -> e1 -> ... -> ek = m         4, def. of ->*
6. k = 0 would force m = abs(n); abs(n) is not a value (O4, line 1),
   contradicting value(m). Hence k >= 1.      4, 5
7. abs(n) -> e1 (5) and abs(n) -> n (2); one-step results from
   abs(n) are unique (O5), hence e1 = n.      2, 5, O5
8. k >= 2 would force n -> e2, contradicting L1; hence k = 1.
                                              5, L1
9. m = ek = e1 = n                            5, 8
10. (abs(n) ->* m & value(m)) => m = n        4-9, =>I
11. n >= 0 => forall m. (...)                 1-10, =>I
[]  (Spec property P2 discharged.)

O7 (VALUE-CORR-NEG):  n < 0 => ((abs(n) ->* m & value(m)) => m = -n)

1. [n < 0]                                    Assumption
2. abs(n) -> -n                               R-ABS-NEG (side cond. 1)
3. abs(n) ->* -n                              2, CL3   (-n is a literal, AF6)
4. [abs(n) ->* m & value(m)]                  Assumption
5. abs(n) = e0 -> e1 -> ... -> ek = m         4, def. of ->*
6. k >= 1, as in O6 line 6.                   4, 5, O4 line 1
7. abs(n) -> e1 (5) and abs(n) -> -n (2); uniqueness by O5 gives
   e1 = -n.                                   2, 5, O5
8. k = 1, as in O6 line 8.                    5, L1
9. m = -n                                     5, 8
10. n < 0 => forall m. (...)                  1-9, =>I
[]  (Spec property P3 discharged.)

O8 (NON-NEGATIVITY):  (abs(n) ->* m & value(m)) => m >= 0

1. [abs(n) ->* m & value(m)]                  Assumption
2. n >= 0 | n < 0                             O2
3. Case n >= 0:
   3.1 m = n                                  O6 with 1
   3.2 m >= 0                                 3.1, case hypothesis
4. Case n < 0:
   4.1 m = -n                                 O7 with 1
   4.2 -n > 0                                 AF4, case hypothesis
   4.3 m >= 0                                 4.1, 4.2, AF5
5. m >= 0                                     2, 3-4, |E
6. forall n m. (...)                          1-5, =>I, forallI
[]  (Spec property P1 discharged.)

O9 (TERMINATION-ABS):  forall n. exists m. abs(n) ->* m (in one step)

1. [n in Z]                                   Assumption
2. n >= 0 | n < 0                             O2
3. Case n >= 0: abs(n) -> n                   R-ABS-POS
4. Case n < 0:  abs(n) -> -n                  R-ABS-NEG
5. exists m. abs(n) ->* m, in one step        2-4, |E, CL3, existsI
6. m is a literal, hence a normal form        L1
7. forall n. exists m. abs(n) ->* m           1-6, forallI
[]

O10 (CONGRUENCE-LIFTING) — STATUS: OPEN AS STATED; REVISED AND PROVED

Attempt of O10 as listed ("e ->* n  =>  abs(e) ->* n"):
1. [e = n = -3, e ->* n in zero steps]        instance of the premise
2. abs(-3) ->* 2                              O7 (n = -3 < 0)
3. the result 2 is not -3                     arithmetic
4. the claimed conclusion abs(e) ->* n fails  counterexample to O10
Status: the obligation as listed is false and cannot be proved. The
intended obligation, already assumed by O10a/O10b of obligations.txt
and required by O11, is:

    O10':  forall e. e ->* n  =>  abs(e) ->* abs(n)

obligations.txt has been amended accordingly (statement of O10).

Proof of O10' (IND on the length k of the reduction e ->* n):
1. [e ->* n]                                  Assumption
2. Case k = 0: e = n.  abs(n) ->* abs(n)      CL1
3. Case k = k' + 1: e = e0 -> e1 ->* n, the tail having length k'.
   3.1 abs(e1) ->* abs(n)                     IH
   3.2 abs(e0) -> abs(e1)                     S-ABS
   3.3 abs(e) ->* abs(n)                      3.1, 3.2, CL2
4. abs(e) ->* abs(n)                          2-3, IND
5. e ->* n => abs(e) ->* abs(n)               1-4, =>I
6. forall e. ...                              5, forallI
[]  (O10 discharged in its revised form O10'.)

O11 (SPEC-ASSEMBLY)

1. [e ->* n]                                  Assumption
2. abs(e) ->* abs(n)                          O10', 1
3. exists m. (abs(n) ->* m & value(m))        O9
4. [abs(n) ->* m & value(m)]                  Assumption (for existsE)
5. m >= 0                                     O8, 4        (P1)
6. n >= 0 | n < 0                             O2
7. Case n >= 0: m = n                         O6, 4        (P2)
8. Case n < 0:  m = -n                        O7, 4        (P3)
9. abs(e) ->* m & m >= 0 & (m = n if n >= 0, m = -n otherwise)
                                              2, 4, 5-8, &I, CL2
10. exists m. (...)                           4-9, existsI
11. e ->* n => exists m. (...)                1-10, =>I
12. forall e. ...                             11, forallI
[]

O0 (ADEQUACY)

1. O0 is the statement derived at line 12 of O11: for every e ->* n
   there is m with abs(e) ->* m, m >= 0, and m = n if n >= 0,
   otherwise m = -n — exactly properties P1-P3 of spec.txt.
2. O0                                         1 (identity)
[]

6. STATUS SUMMARY

    O1   proved            (O1a definitional; O1b by intersection)
    O2   proved            (AF1, AF5)
    O3   proved            (AF2, AF3)
    O4   proved            (L2, O2)
    O5   proved            (L3)
    O6   proved            (P2 discharged)
    O7   proved            (P3 discharged)
    O8   proved            (P1 discharged)
    O9   proved            (O2, L1)
    O10  revised + proved  (as listed the statement is false;
                          counterexample abs(-3) ->* 2, which is
                          not -3; repaired to O10' and proved;
                          obligations.txt amended)
    O11  proved            (O10', O9, O8, O2, O6, O7)
    O0   proved            (via O11)

    After the O10 revision, no obligation remains open.
","path":"proof.txt"}

{"content":"Proofs of the Obligations in obligations.txt — Natural Deduction

1. PRELIMINARIES

1.1 Notation
    e, e0, ...   expressions            n, m          integer literals
    value(e)     e is a literal         ->, ->*       as in semantics.txt
    [phi]        assumption phi         []            end of proof
    ND rules:    &I &E  (and intro/elim),  |I |E  (or intro/elim),
                 =>I =>E (implication),    ~I ~E  (negation),
                 forallI forallE,          existsI existsE,
                 RAA (reductio),           IND (structural induction),
                 |E with cited subproofs for each disjunct.
    Notation for formulas: & = and, | = or, ~ = not, => = implies.

1.2 Closure lemmas for ->* (by definition of the reflexive-
    transitive closure; used without further comment)
    CL1  e ->* e                                  (reflexivity)
    CL2  e ->* f & f ->* g  =>  e ->* g           (transitivity)
    CL3  e -> f  =>  e ->* f                      (monotonicity)

1.3 Background facts about Z (standard ordered-ring properties,
    used as premises)
    AF1  (trichotomy)          forall n in Z:  n < 0 | n = 0 | n > 0
    AF2  (irreflexivity)       forall n:  ~(n < n)
    AF3  (mixed transitivity)  a < b & b <= c  =>  a < c
    AF4  (negation reverses)   n < 0  =>  -n > 0
    AF5  (definition of >=)    n >= 0  <=>  n > 0 | n = 0
    AF6  (totality)            + and unary - are total functions on
                               Z with unique results; hence n1 + n2
                               and -n are literals of Expr.

    Remark: the grammar of semantics.txt has no variables, so every
    expression is closed.

2. LEMMA L1 (VALUE-IRREDUCIBILITY)

    L1:  forall n. ~exists e'. n -> e'

1. [n -> e']                                  Assumption
2. A derivation of n -> e' ends in a rule whose conclusion's left
   side matches the literal n. Left sides of the rules (sec. 3,
   semantics.txt): abs(e) [S-ABS], e1 + e2 [S-ADD-L], n + e2
   [S-ADD-R], n1 + n2 [R-ADD], abs(n) [R-ABS-POS/NEG]. None is a
   literal.                                   rule schemas
3. No rule instance has left side n; no derivation exists.   2
4. F                                          1, 3
5. ~exists e'. n -> e'                        1-4, ~I
6. forall n. ~exists e'. n -> e'              5, forallI
[]

3. OBLIGATIONS O1, O2, O3

O1a (side conditions well-formed)
1. The side conditions are "n >= 0", "n < 0", "n3 = n1 + n2":
   atomic formulas of first-order arithmetic with all variables
   ranging over Z.                            sec. 3, semantics.txt
2. Each is a well-formed proposition.         1, definitional
[]

O1b (smallest rule-closed relation exists)
1. Let R = { S subset of Expr x Expr : S is closed under all rules }.
2. Expr x Expr is in R: for any rule instance with true side
   condition and premises in Expr x Expr, the conclusion is an
   element of Expr x Expr.                    trivially
3. R is nonempty.                             2
4. ->  :=  intersection of R.                 3, set comprehension
5. -> is closed under the rules: given premises in -> and a true
   side condition, the conclusion lies in every S in R (each S is
   closed), hence in the intersection.        4, definition of intersection
6. -> is the smallest such relation: any closed S satisfies
   intersection of R subset of S.             4, definition of intersection
7. -> exists and is smallest.                 2-6, existsI
[]  (O1 discharged by O1a and O1b.)

O2 (CASE-COVERAGE):  forall n in Z. n >= 0 | n < 0

1. [n in Z]                                   Assumption
2. n < 0 | n = 0 | n > 0                      AF1
3. Case n < 0:   n < 0                        right disjunct, |I
4. Case n = 0:   n >= 0                       2 (n = 0), AF5, =-substitution
5. Case n > 0:   n >= 0                       AF5
6. n >= 0 | n < 0                             2-5, |E
7. forall n in Z. n >= 0 | n < 0              1-6, forallI
[]

O3 (CASE-DISJOINTNESS):  forall n. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)

1. [n >= 0 & n < 0]                           Assumption
2. n >= 0, i.e. 0 <= n                        &E 1
3. n < 0                                      &E 1
4. n < n                                      AF3 on 3, 2
5. ~(n < n)                                   AF2
6. F                                          4, 5, ~E
7. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)                          1-6, ~I
8. forall n. ~(n >= 0 & n < 0)                7, forallI
[]

4. LEMMAS L2, L3

L2 (PROGRESS-EXPR):  forall e. value(e) | exists e'. e -> e'
    Proof by IND on e.

Case e = n:
1. value(n)                                   def. of value
2. value(n) | exists e'. n -> e'              1, |I

Case e = abs(e0), with IH: value(e0) | exists e'. e0 -> e':
1. Case value(e0), i.e. e0 = n:
   1.1 n >= 0 | n < 0                         O2
   1.2 Case n >= 0: abs(n) -> n               R-ABS-POS
       Case n < 0:  abs(n) -> -n              R-ABS-NEG
   1.3 exists e'. abs(e0) -> e'               1.2, |E, existsI
   1.4 disjunction                            1.3, |I
2. Case e0 -> e0':  abs(e0) -> abs(e0')       S-ABS
   existsI; |I
3. value(abs(e0)) | exists e'. abs(e0) -> e'  1-2, |E

Case e = e1 + e2, with IH(e1), IH(e2):
1. Case e1 -> e1':  e1 + e2 -> e1' + e2       S-ADD-L; existsI; |I
2. Case value(e1), i.e. e1 = n1:
   2.1 Case e2 -> e2': n1 + e2 -> n1 + e2'    S-ADD-R; existsI; |I
   2.2 Case value(e2), i.e. e2 = n2:
       n1 + n2 -> n3, where n3 = n1 + n2      R-ADD, AF6 (totality)
       existsI; |I
3. disjunction                                1-2, |E

All three cases give the disjunction; IND discharges the induction.
[]

L3 (DETERMINISM-EXPR):  forall e a b. (e -> a & e -> b) => a = b
    Proof by IND on e, with case analysis on applicable rules.

Case e = n:
1. [n -> a & n -> b]                          Assumption
2. F                                          1, L1 (no step from n)
3. a = b                                      2, RAA (vacuous)

Case e = abs(e0), with IH for e0. Rules matching abs(_): S-ABS,
R-ABS-POS, R-ABS-NEG.
1. Case value(e0), i.e. e0 = n:
   1.1 S-ABS inapplicable: its premise n -> c contradicts L1.

       its conclusion is fully determined (n, resp. -n). Hence
       a = b.
2. Case ~value(e0):
   2.1 R-ABS-POS/NEG inapplicable: their schemas require the
       argument to be a literal; e0 is not. (schema mismatch)
   2.2 Only S-ABS applies: a = abs(c), b = abs(d) with e0 -> c,
       e0 -> d.
   2.3 c = d                                  IH
   2.4 a = b                                  2.2, 2.3

Case e = e1 + e2, with IH for e1, e2. Rules matching _ + _: S-ADD-L,
S-ADD-R, R-ADD.
1. Case ~value(e1): only S-ADD-L applies (S-ADD-R and R-ADD require
   e1 to be a literal). a = c + e2, b = d + e2 with e1 -> c,
   e1 -> d; c = d by IH; hence a = b.
2. Case e1 = n1, ~value(e2): S-ADD-L blocked (premise n1 -> _
   contradicts L1); only S-ADD-R: a = b = n1 + e2' (uniqueness of
   e2' by IH).
3. Case e1 = n1, e2 = n2: S-ADD-L and S-ADD-R blocked by L1; only
   R-ADD: a = n1 + n2 = b by AF6 (functionality).

All cases: a = b; IND discharges the induction.
[]
